passage: On his fourth day in Delhi, Jomon had already ridden the metro end to end twice, just to watch the stations change. He ate chole kulche from a cart outside the college gate, burned his tongue and laughed. His hostel room smelled of fresh paint; he stuck a city map on the wall and circled places with a red pen. Avni, a second-year who ran the photography club, invited him on a Sunday walk through the old city, and he said yes before she finished. Amma called every night from Kottayam. 'Are you eating? Are you sleeping?' 'Amma, everything is so busy here, I'll call tomorrow,' he said, already pulling on his shoes. Only once, lying in bed with the fan clicking, did he think of the smell of rain on their veranda, and then the club's group chat buzzed and he forgot.

qa.q: Where did Avni invite Jomon to go?
qa.a: On a Sunday walk through the old city.

qa.q: What does Jomon riding the metro end to end suggest about his feelings?
qa.a: He is thrilled by everything new in the city and full of restless energy 🎉

qa.q: What could help Jomon now, while the city still feels exciting?
qa.a: Keeping a short regular call with Amma even on busy days would give him a steady link to home for when the newness wears off.

qa.q: What might Amma be feeling when Jomon rushes off the phone?
qa.a: Amma may miss him and feel a little shut out, while also being glad he sounds so happy.

grounding: Shows a new student's honeymoon days in a new city, where excitement and activity push aside a brief moment of missing home.

passage:
'Look at this!' Salma held up a paper bag of pastries. 'Forty pence each at the market. Forty!'
Elizabeth, her new flatmate, laughed from the top bunk. 'You've said that about everything today.'
'Because everything is amazing. The trams! The library has a whole floor just for maps!'
'Did you call your family?'
'Tomorrow. Tonight there's the international students' quiz. You're coming.'
'I've got seminar reading...'
'Elizabeth. Quiz. Free pizza.'
'Fine.' Elizabeth climbed down. 'Your phone's buzzing, by the way.'
Salma glanced at it: Ammi, missed call, the third one. She typed, 'All good, so busy, love you ❤️,' and pocketed it. For a second her face went still. Then she grabbed her scarf. 'Come on, we'll be late. I want to see the canal at night too.'

qa.q: How much did the pastries cost at the market?
What might Salma's face going still for a second suggest?
qa.a: It hints at a moment of homesickness that Salma quickly pushes aside with the rush of plans.

qa.q: What small step could help Salma keep her energy and her link to home?
qa.a: She could set a short regular time to call Ammi, so home stays close while she keeps exploring.

qa.q: How does Elizabeth see Salma's first days?
qa.a: Elizabeth finds Salma's excitement funny and catching, and ends up coming to the quiz.

grounding: Illustrates the excitement of first days in a new city, with a missed call from home brushed aside by a rush of activity.
